original_text: Value of Biodiversity¨Provision of Fresh Water¤The water cycle provides fresh water to terrestrial ecosystems¤Humans use this fresh water in innumerable ways¤Freshwater ecosystems provide us with a large diversity of species we can use as a source of food¤Forests and some other natural ecosystems soak up water and release it at a regular rate, thereby reducing flooding¨Prevention of Soil Erosion¤Intact ecosystems naturally retain soil and prevent soil erosion¤The importance of this attribute is particularly observed after deforestation¨Regulation of Climate¤Trees provide shade and reduce the need for fans and air conditioners in the summer¤Globally, forests restore the climate by incorporating carbon dioxide from the atmosphere¤Reduction of forests reduces the carbon dioxide uptake and oxygen output through Photosynthesis¨Ecotourism¤In the United States, nearly $4 billion is spent on fees, travel, lodging, and food within natural settings¤Many underdeveloped countries in tropical regions take advantage of this by offering “ecotours” of the local biodiversity
explanation: This slide details indirect values of biodiversity: 1) Provision of Fresh Water: the water cycle supplies fresh water, and ecosystems like forests act as sponges to absorb rain and release it slowly, mitigating flooding. 2) Prevention of Soil Erosion: intact root networks anchor soil; deforestation severely increases erosion. 3) Climate Regulation: locally, trees provide shade, reducing cooling energy needs; globally, forests act as carbon sinks, taking up CO2 and releasing O2 via photosynthesis. 4) Ecotourism: in the US, individuals spend nearly $4 billion annually traveling to natural areas, and many developing nations generate significant revenue by offering ecotours of their biodiversity.

questions.q: How do intact forests reduce the severity of flooding?
opts: They block the windward side of mountain ranges completely.
They soak up water and release it at a regular rate rather than letting it run off all at once.
They speed up the evaporation of oceans.
They convert water into inorganic phosphate.
questions.exp: The notes state that 'Forests and some other natural ecosystems soak up water and release it at a regular rate, thereby reducing flooding.'

questions.q: What is the global climate effect of reducing forest cover?
opts: It increases local shade and cools the Earth.
It reduces carbon dioxide uptake and oxygen output through photosynthesis.
It decreases the rate of cellular respiration in soils.
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Reduction of forests reduces the carbon dioxide uptake and oxygen output through Photosynthesis.'
